title: openvino : match GPU device by family, not exact "GPU" name
body:
## Overview

Fixes https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/29235. The device name is "GPU.N" on a multi-GPU machine while backend compares against "GPU" string.

Changes consist of three related and non-splittable fixes in OpenVINO backend:
- A proper handling of "GPU.N" name.
- The proper handling required also getting the proper device by UUID and proper platform for the selected device.
- Handling initialization errors required adding abort on startup instead of causing UB later.

## Additional information

### Comparing against "GPU" fix

This is the most important part. See all details and possible consequences in the https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/29235

### Using the hardcoded platform and device fix

When code selects from multiple available devices, then also multiple platforms are possible. clGetExtensionFunctionAddressForPlatform was always called on the first OpenCL platform, while device used can be on another. Because numbering of devices in OpenVINO and in OpenCL may be different - matching by UUID is now used to select right device and its platform.

This fix could not be left to another PR because fixing just "GPU" name problem would introduce regression. This is because the whole code block creating OpenCL context is currently dead code on multi-GPU OpenVINO backend (under false `if (device_name == "GPU")` condition). The first fix enables this code and without the fix it could be possible that OpenCL context be created on wrong device causing inference running on one GPU with KV cache on another.

### Running after failed init fix

Two above fixes modify `init` code which required proper error handling. Previously on init errors backend continued to run causing undefined behavior. Using abort instead as it is consistent with other backends and there is no clean fallback possible when user requested running on exact GPU and it can not run.

## Verification

Used OpenVINO 2026.5 (master).

### Correctness verification

Ran `test-backend-ops` in both runs:
- all GPUs master except one, master bracch - "GPU" name is used
- no GPUs masked, PR branch - "GPU.N" name is used

Numbers of ok/failed/not-supported tests are the same in each of 14 groups of tests. Perfect parity. "GPU.N" started to behave exactly as "GPU". Previously running with name "GPU.N" resulted in exceptions and large errors (see issue for details). See table below:

| Op | Filter | ok | fail | not supported |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POOL_2D | all | 56 | 0 | 72 |
| MUL_MAT | type_a=mxfp4, | 18 | 0 | 61 |
| MUL_MAT | type_a=bf16, | 14 | 0 | 137 |
| MUL_MAT | type_a=f16, | 197 | 0 | 84 |
| MUL_MAT_ID | type_a=f16, | 0 | 0 | 93 |
| MUL_MAT_ID | type_a=f32, | 0 | 0 | 73 |
| MUL_MAT_ID | type_a=bf16, | 0 | 0 | 7 |
| MUL_MAT_ID | type_a=q8_0, | 0 | 0 | 75 |
| MUL_MAT_ID | type_a=q4_K, | 0 | 0 | 84 |
| MUL_MAT_ID | type_a=mxfp4, | 0 | 0 | 74 |
| GET_ROWS | all | 35 | 0 | 205 |
| DIV | all | 81 | 0 | 10 |
| CONCAT | all | 52 | 0 | 140 |
| REPEAT | all | 14 | 0 | 4 |

Commands used
```
# master, iGPU hidden, so the Arc is the plain "GPU"
ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0 GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU  test-backend-ops test -b OPENVINO0 -o MUL_MAT_ID -p type_a=f16,

# branch, both GPUs visible, so the Arc is "GPU.1"
GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU.1                   test-backend-ops test -b OPENVINO0 -o MUL_MAT_ID -p type_a=f16,
```
Command then repeated with different `-o` and `-p` params for each group (row).

#### Note 

The branch moves from GPU to CPU some cases which were by chance passing under `GPU.N` name. The total number is 252 cases, the largest being MUL_MAT_ID type_a=mxfp4 with 74 cases. Now this matches behavior which master has for "GPU" name.

### Performance verification

#### decode

One of the https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/29235 consequences is performance drop in decode phase (point 5 in "Steps to reproduce" there). See below table to see confirmation that decoding on large context under name "GPU.1" gets back to what is observed when name "GPU" is used. Column *branch GPU.1* matching *master GPU* proves this.

At the same time column *master GPU.1* compared to *branch GPU.1* shows a speedup which user not aware of masked GPUs workaround will observe.

Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M, Intel Arc Pro B70, median of 5, tok/s

| Test | master GPU.1 | branch GPU.1 | speedup | master GPU | branch GPU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tg128 @ d128 | 48.9 | 64.6 | 1.32x | 63.4 | 62.0 |
| tg128 @ d4096 | 9.9 | 46.5 | 4.68x | 47.5 | 46.7 |

Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-Q4_K_M, same conditions

| Test | master GPU.1 | branch GPU.1 | speedup | master GPU | branch GPU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tg128 @ d128 | 20.6 | 32.8 | 1.59x | 31.6 | 31.7 |
| tg128 @ d4096 | 3.4 | 21.2 | 6.22x | 20.1 | 20.1 |


Commands to use in order to repeat measurements
```
M=$HOME/models/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf
A="-m $M --device OPENVINO0 -ngl 999 -b 512 -ub 512 -p 512 -n 128 -d 128,4096 -r 5"

# columns "master GPU.1" and "branch GPU.1", run on each build
GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU.1                   llama-bench $A

# columns "master GPU" and "branch GPU": the iGPU is hidden, so the same Arc
# answers to the plain "GPU" name. Use a mask valid on your machine.
ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0 GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU  llama-bench $A
```
Note: `-b 512 -ub 512` are required because current master fails with `failed to decode prompt batch, res = -3` on OpenVINO backend for batches larger than 512.

#### Prefill

Including prefill results for completeness. For prefill the change in this PR should be neutral when we compare *branch GPU.1*, *master GPU* and *branch GPU* columns and it is. All ranges overlap, so difference in medians is noise.

On the other hand it should improve case between *master GPU.1* and *branch GPU.1* which is visible above noise in the last *pp512 @ d4096* case.

Prompt processing, median of 5 with min-max in brackets, tok/s

Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M

| Test | master GPU.1 | branch GPU.1 | master GPU | branch GPU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pp512 @ d128 | 6141 (5457-6354) | 7282 (4300-7466) | 7204 (6887-7653) | 6761 (6405-7006) |
| pp512 @ d4096 | 2700 (2244-2833) | 3581 (2688-4047) | 3583 (2761-4061) | 4056 (2725-4066) |

Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-Q4_K_M

| Test | master GPU.1 | branch GPU.1 | master GPU | branch GPU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pp512 @ d128 | 2790 (2649-2793) | 2962 (2259-3178) | 3080 (2695-3579) | 3247 (2654-3552) |
| pp512 @ d4096 | **967 (892-991)** | **1724 (1355-1798)** | 1642 (1374-1802) | 1512 (1071-1565) |

#### No regression for current users

Using "GPU" name on either master or branch shows no difference (values close each other inside one column). This was checked more precisely on a separate tests session by alternating runs.

Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M, other GPUs masked so the Arc Pro B70 is the plain "GPU", alternating runs, tok/s

| Run order | tg128 @ d128 | tg128 @ d4096 | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| master, 1st | 64.1 | 48.0 | warm-up, slower |
| branch, 2nd | 67.8 | 48.1 | |
| branch, 3rd | 68.1 | 48.8 | |
| master, 4th | 68.4 | 48.9 | |


## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: Cursor IDE was used to write code under my guidance and verification with multiple changes requested by me or written by hand by me during course of coding. AI was used for measuring fix performance impact under my guidance. This PR description was written by hand by me with tables containing numbers prepared by AI after its performance measurements. Code change is fully understood and maintainable by me.

The motivation for this is that for large models it can take a long time to run them models, and especially for the original model which seldom changes this is very time consuming. title: ggml-sycl : fix VMM pool pinning VRAM and collapse performance when the model does not fit
body:
## Overview
Fixes SYCL VMM pool behavior when the model does not fit in physical VRAM.

The VMM pool keeps committed physical pages for the lifetime of the pool. When temporary allocations reach a size that does not fit in physical VRAM, the driver can spill the committed pages into shared system memory, causing a severe performance drop.

This change makes VMM allocation failure non-fatal by falling back to direct USM allocation, and disables the VMM pool by default.

## Additional information

### Changes

* Fall back to direct USM allocation when a VMM commit fails instead of failing the whole operation.

  * Fallback allocations are tracked so that `free()` uses the corresponding allocation API.
* Disable the VMM pool by default with `GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_VMM=0`.

  * The VMM pool can still be enabled explicitly through the environment variable.

### Performance impact

Measured with Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B Q4_K_M on an Intel Arc B570 with `-ngl 99`:

* Prompt processing with the VMM pool enabled: **0.7 t/s**
* Prompt processing with the VMM pool disabled: **6.2 t/s**

Note: the memory overflow (staging into shared system memory) itself occurs in both builds when the model does not fit in physical VRAM with `-ngl 99`. The official build stages through `sycl::malloc_device` and reaches approximately **25 t/s generation** on the same setup; the VMM pool pinning makes it several times worse. Models that fit in physical VRAM are not affected: the 9B model runs normally with `-ngl 99`, and `-ngl auto` does not overflow.

The GPU memory usage was measured with the Windows GPU performance counters while running the same model with the VMM pool disabled: total committed 20.9 GB, of which 8.6 GB was dedicated (VRAM) and 13.2 GB was non-local (shared system memory) - the staging behavior was observed directly.

### Stability

Running with the VMM pool enabled and a model exceeding physical VRAM was also observed to restart the host system (driver-level instability). The staging state brings the system memory close to its limit, where the process being killed was observed. This further motivates disabling the pool by default.

### Related issue

A memory/access-violation crash in `igdrcl64.dll` was also observed when OpenCL GPUs were enumerated with `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR` unset. The device enumeration changes in the separate de-dpct work prioritize Level Zero devices and remove that path.

See #29229

## Requirements

* I have read and agree to the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

* AI usage disclosure: **YES - GLM-5.3 Flash via OpenCode was used for analysis, implementation, routine edits, and debugging assistance. The author identified the issue and provided the overall direction for the fix.**

title: cuda: fix the q8_0 and iq4_nl dequantization kernels
body:
## Overview

<!-- TODO(author): describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
Two fixes to the `ggml-cuda` dequantization kernels:
- `dequantize_block_q8_0_f16` is guarded by `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL`. MUSA's `mcc` defines `__MUSA_ARCH__` in the device pass and not `__CUDA_ARCH__`, so the condition is false, the body is dropped and the kernel is launched empty — every `q8_0` dequantization produces garbage. Also guard on `__MUSA_ARCH__`; NVIDIA builds are unaffected because `defined(__MUSA_ARCH__)` is false there.
- `dequantize_block_iq4_nl` writes `QK_K` values per block, but an `IQ4_NL` row is only guaranteed to be a multiple of `QK4_NL`, and ops such as `MUL_MAT` do use shorter rows. Threads whose 32-value sub-block starts at or past the end of the row were reading and writing past the end of the output. Skip those sub-blocks. For rows that are a multiple of `QK_K` the check never fires.
Both were found with `test-backend-ops` on an MTT S5000 (MUSA architecture `31`); the `q8_0` case is MUSA specific, the `iq4_nl` case is backend independent.

title: metal : wide query tile for kernel_flash_attn_ext
body:
## Overview

The current flash-attention kernel processes 8 query rows for each K/V tile it loads. The main idea in this PR is to reuse that same K/V data for 16 query rows instead, so each K/V load does twice as much query work.

`kernel_flash_attn_ext` already takes the number of queries per threadgroup `Q` as a template parameter, but the QK^T and P*V simdgroup-matrix blocks only process the first 8 query rows, and only `Q = 8` is instantiated. This PR makes those blocks iterate over all `Q/8` query blocks and adds `Q = 16` with `nsg = 4` and `nsg = 8`.

Whether the 16-row tile is faster depends on the device and shape, so it is selected through the tuning table, like `fa_vec_pick`. Only `GGML_METAL_DEVICE_M5` has rows in this PR, and M5 is not a family representative, so other devices keep the existing dispatch.

The first version of this PR used a shape-only gate and always ran the 16-row tile with `nsg = 8`. That regressed on M4 Max (see @forforever73's table below), so the gate was replaced by the tuning table as suggested.

---

### Dispatch

`ggml_metal_tuning::fa_pick` maps `(device, DK, DV, ne11 bucket)` to `(Q, NSG)`. It first looks for an exact `ne11` bucket, then a `FA_NE11_DEFAULT` row, first for the device and then for its family representative.

If nothing matches, the existing dispatch is used. M5 is not the representative of any family, so its 25 rows are not used by another device.

The 8-row tile is always used when:

* `ne01 < 64`
* `ne01 < 256` and the last wide tile would hold only 1..8 rows. It would pad 8 more rows than the 8-row tile, which costs 2–4% at KV 4096 on M5 (`ne01 = 68`: 0.96x).
* K/V are not F16 and are not dequantized to F16 up front through `use_kv_f16`. BF16/F32 K/V and the in-kernel dequantization branches are unchanged.
* `GGML_PAD(DV, 64) % (16*NSG) != 0`
* The threadgroup memory would exceed the device limit (320/256 and 576/512 at 32 KiB).

The wide tile is only instantiated for the F16 kernels, which keeps library load time close to master. A cold compile of the `fa` library with an empty shader cache goes from 13.6 s to 14.2 s on M5. The `blk` buffer stays sized for the 8-row tile, which is an upper bound for the 16-row one.

---

### Tuning

`ggml-metal-tuning fa` generates the table rows. The sweep took about 20 minutes on M5.

The tuner compares the 8-row tile against `Q = 16` with `nsg = 4` and `nsg = 8`, using F16 K/V and GQA 8. GQA 8 had the smallest gains in the measurements below. The sweep covers 13 head sizes, 8 KV lengths from 512 to 65536, and up to 4 batch sizes, including a partial last tile.

A bucket gets a row only if the candidate is no slower than the 8-row tile at every sampled point and at least 2% faster overall. `nsg = 8` is selected over `nsg = 4` only when it is at least 3% faster. On M5, hs 96, 192, and 256 lose at some point with KV < 4096 and get no row there.

`nsg` is part of the table because no single value works for every head size. `Q = 8` with `nsg = 8` is slower than master's `Q = 8, nsg = 4` in every case measured on M5 (0.77–0.99x).

For `Q = 16`, geometric mean speedup vs master over the tuner's 30 sample points per head size is:

| Head | `Q = 16, nsg = 4` | `Q = 16, nsg = 8` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 64/64 | 1.166 (0) | 1.007 (2) |
| 128/128 | 1.166 (0) | 1.147 (0) |
| 256/256 | 1.035 (13) | 1.099 (3) |

> *The number in parentheses denotes the count of sampled points slower than master.*

With `nsg = 4`, hs 256 loses at almost every point with KV $\le$ 4096 (0.89–1.00x). With `nsg = 8`, hs 64 gains almost nothing. The three hs 256 points where `nsg = 8` loses are at KV < 4096, where hs 256 gets no row. Master's `nsg = ne00 >= 512 ? 8 : 4` still applies to the 8-row tile.

Whether `Q = 16` helps on M4 Max requires running the tuner on that hardware. A device only uses the wide tile once it has rows in `fa_tuned_table`, and a run that emits nothing indicates it should stay on the 8-row tile. Rows for other devices can be added once profiled.

---

### Adding a Device

To generate rows for another Metal device:

1. **Build the tuner and test targets:**
```sh
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j --target ggml-metal-tuning test-backend-ops llama-bench

```


2. **Run the tuner:**
```sh
./build/bin/ggml-metal-tuning fa > fa_rows.txt 2> fa_sweep.log

```


* Takes ~20 minutes on M5.
* `fa_rows.txt` contains rows ready to add to `fa_tuned_table`. An empty file indicates the wide tile did not outperform the baseline.
* `fa_sweep.log` contains detailed per-point measurements.


3. **Verify correctness and benchmark:**
```sh
# Correctness check
./build/bin/test-backend-ops test -b MTL0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT

# Microbenchmarks
./build/bin/test-backend-ops perf -b MTL0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT -p 'nb=4096,'

# End-to-end performance
./build/bin/llama-bench -m <model> -fa 1 -ub 2048 -p 2048 \
  -d 0,2048,4096,8192,16384,32768 -r 1 -n 32 -t 1

```



> **Note:** The tuner prints the device token near the start of `fa_sweep.log`. If the device reports `GGML_METAL_DEVICE_GENERIC`, it must be explicitly defined in `ggml_metal_device_id` first to prevent generic rows from matching unspecified hardware.

---

### Performance

**Hardware:** Apple M5 (10-core GPU, 24 GB)

**Baseline:** Master `ec9281505`

*All results use the `(Q, NSG)` selected by the M5 tuning rows.*

```sh
./build/bin/test-backend-ops perf -b MTL0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT -p 'nb=4096,'

```

Speedup in % (positive = PR is faster). Values represent the median of three paired runs per case:

| hs / GQA | kv = 4096 | kv = 8192 | kv = 16384 | kv = 32768 | kv = 65536 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **hs64 / g1** | +16.0% | +33.1% | +53.5% | +66.2% | +72.2% |
| **hs64 / g4** | +13.3% | +16.2% | +25.1% | +41.8% | +52.9% |
| **hs64 / g8** | +12.7% | +15.3% | +22.0% | +35.0% | +47.8% |
| **hs128 / g1** | +20.1% | +35.3% | +41.4% | +46.7% | +36.2% |
| **hs128 / g4** | +9.9% | +23.7% | +33.0% | +35.8% | +29.8% |
| **hs128 / g8** | +10.8% | +19.9% | +32.5% | +34.6% | +30.8% |
| **hs256 / g1** | +18.4% | +28.0% | +41.5% | +59.5% | +66.0% |
| **hs256 / g4** | +18.9% | +19.0% | +23.6% | +19.1% | +26.3% |
| **hs256 / g8** | +18.8% | +18.9% | +22.0% | +16.3% | +22.2% |

* The speedup is largest without GQA, remaining positive across all head sizes and context lengths on M5.
* At hs 256 and KV 65536, the 16-row tile executes in 54–57 ms per query head regardless of GQA. The 8-row tile requires 62–67 ms with shared K/V heads and ~100 ms when unshared.
* For shapes remaining on the 8-row tile, `DK/DV = 576/512` shows a delta of +0.2% to +4.6% (mostly under +2%). Forcing `gpt-oss-20b` onto the 8-row tile yields 0.99–1.00x end-to-end at all context depths.

---

### End-to-End Benchmarks

```sh
./build/bin/llama-bench -m <model> -fa 1 -ub 2048 -p 2048 -d 0,2048,4096,8192,16384,32768 -r 1 -n 32 -t 1

```

*Values represent the mean of two alternating runs between master and PR. The `d65536` rows were evaluated separately.*

#### Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B IQ3_XXS

*(hs 256, GQA 8, full attention in 1 of 4 layers)*

| Test | Master (t/s) | PR (t/s) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pp2048` | 732.93 | 739.45 | **1.009x** |
| `pp2048@d2048` | 661.59 | 671.37 | **1.015x** |
| `pp2048@d4096` | 600.04 | 624.41 | **1.041x** |
| `pp2048@d8192` | 508.65 | 536.88 | **1.055x** |
| `pp2048@d16384` | 393.45 | 426.27 | **1.083x** |
| `pp2048@d32768` | 261.73 | 284.72 | **1.088x** |
| `pp2048@d65536` | 155.11 | 173.97 | **1.122x** |

#### Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M

*(hs 256, GQA 4, full attention in 1 of 4 layers)*

| Test | Master (t/s) | PR (t/s) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pp2048` | 358.91 | 371.39 | **1.035x** |
| `pp2048@d2048` | 349.64 | 352.77 | **1.009x** |
| `pp2048@d4096` | 337.12 | 335.91 | **0.996x** |
| `pp2048@d8192` | 309.03 | 320.37 | **1.037x** |

title: llama-bench: fix default thread count on NUMA systems
body:
## Overview

`cmd_params_defaults` is a static const struct initialized at file scope. Its `n_threads` field is set by calling `common_cpu_get_num_math()` during static initialization, before `main()` runs. On Linux NUMA systems where `numactl` is used to restrict CPU affinity, the affinity isn't active yet at this point, so the wrong thread count gets captured. For example, it can end up using all cores across both sockets instead of only the socket assigned by `numactl`.

This changes two lines in `tools/llama-bench/llama-bench.cpp`:

* `parse_cmd_params()`: call `common_cpu_get_num_math()` at runtime when `-t` isn't supplied, instead of using the stale value from `cmd_params_defaults.n_threads`.
* `print_usage()`: do the same so `--help` also shows the correct runtime default.

Fixes #17611.

## Additional information

PR #23905 addresses the same root cause. The difference is in how `print_usage()` is handled: that PR replaces the default with a hardcoded string `"auto - determined at runtime via common_cpu_get_num_math()"`, which is inconsistent with every other help line that prints an actual value. This PR instead calls `common_cpu_get_num_math()` directly and prints the real number with `%d`, keeping the output consistent with the rest of the help text.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

title: metal: fix metal tensor kernel_mul_mm error for large tensor
body:
Assisted-by: Codex ## Overview In an experiment, I consistently observed that when the offset between the slice address and the tensor base address is greater than or equal to 2 GB, the actual address produced by the Metal Tensor API's `slice` method differs from the expected address by -4 GB. This change modifies the `kernel_mul_mm` implementation in `ggml/src/ggml-metal/kernels/mul_mm.metal` for the `GGML_METAL_HAS_TENSOR == true` path. Instead of using the `slice` method, it explicitly computes the address of each slice and constructs the tensor directly from the computed address. Related issue: #27784 After this change, the issue is no longer reproducible. ```bash sending long embedding request... long: output_size=1024 invalid_values=0 * Terminal will be reused by tasks, press any key to close it. * Executing task: python3 scripts/issue27784_probe.py sending short embedding request... short: output_size=1024 invalid_values=0 * Terminal will be reused by tasks, press any key to close it. ``` ## Additional information ### Environment Hardware: Apple MacBook Air 13 inch M5 16G macOS: 26.6.2 (25G83) Metal compiler: Apple metal version 32023.883 (metalfe-32023.883), Target: air64-apple-darwin25.6.0, Thread model: posix ### Experiment Design Each case runs the same matrix multiplication with a K dimension of `16`, producing a cooperative tensor `cT`. The only difference between the two dispatches is the storage destination: ```mermaid flowchart TB A["A: K x tile_rows"] --> MM["Tensor API matmul"] B["B: K x tile_columns"] --> MM MM --> CT["cT: tile_rows x tile_columns"] CT --> P1["Path 1: calculate the dstTile pointer first
then tensor(dstTile, tile shape)"] CT --> P2["Path 2: tensor(whole tensor)
then whole.slice(row, column)"] P1 --> R1["direct_values"] P2 --> R2["slice_expected_values
slice_wrapped_values"] ``` Path 1 uses explicit 64-bit address calculation in the host language: ```metal device float * tile = c + (uint64_t) column * m + row; ``` Path 2 wraps the complete output as a two-dimensional tensor: ```metal auto whole = tensor(c, dextents(m, n), array({1, m})); cT.store(whole.slice(row, column)); ``` ### Results | Case | Slice start | Does the tile cross 2 GiB? | Direct path | Correct slice address | Slice -4 GiB address | Conclusion | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | Start 1024 B below | `0x7ffffc00` | No | 256/256 | 256/256 | 0/256 | Correct | | Start 64 B below | `0x7fffffc0` | Yes | 256/256 | 256/256 | 0/256 | Correct | | Half of tile crosses | `0x7ffffe00` | Yes | 256/256 | 256/256 | 0/256 | Correct | | Exactly at boundary | `0x80000000` | No | 256/256 | 0/256 | 256/256 | 4 GiB early | | 64 B above | `0x80000040` | No | 256/256 | 0/256 | 256/256 | 4 GiB early | | 1024 B above | `0x80000400` | No | 256/256 | 0/256 | 256/256 | 4 GiB early | ```mermaid xychart-beta title "16 x 16 tile: slice start versus actual write displacement" x-axis ["-1024 B", "-64 B", "crossing tile", "0 B", "+64 B", "+1024 B"] y-axis "actual address - correct address (GiB)" -4 --> 0 line [0, 0, 0, -4, -4, -4] ``` These results show a step with no transition interval. From `0x7fffffff` to `0x80000000`, the displacement changes directly from 0 to -4 GiB. ## Requirements - I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) - AI usage disclosure: YES, I use codex to help me write experiment script.

title: Enables Windows ARM64 build with MSVC cl.exe
body:
## Overview

In the current flow on WoA systems the default is to build with the `arm64-windows-llvm-release` preset, which requires developers to install clang when building MSVC. This PR allows developers to directly use `cmake -B build -S . -DGGML_NATIVE=ON` to build the project on WoA systems. 

In addition to build with ARM64EC, users can simply do `cmake -S . -B build_arm64ec -A ARM64EC`

## Additional information

For context, several MSVC gaps for NEON intrinsics were identified. 
1. FP16 vector intrinsics not implemented in MSVC
2. dotprod probing volatile issue
3. i8mm probing volatile issue
4. SME/SVE not implemented in MSVC
5. Other Feature detection error with MSVC (such as FMA)

For item 2 and 3, we dropped the volatile keyword in cmake, and for 5 some corresponding cmake changes were added either during flag checking or when probing happens. Additional change is in quant.c to make the syntax conform to MSVC.

However, since item 1, 4 are still pending MSVC support, native MSVC build cannot turn on all of the arm intrinsics support as compared to clang build. So there is performance gap on the CPU backend. 

### Profiling results
For other systems (linux, x86_64 windows), we locally tested and saw no performance degradation between PR and master. 

Local profiling MSVC build vs clang.exe build performance is also on par.

Another thing to note is that MSVC does not define `__NEON_ARM` by default even though there is the arm neon header in MSVC. This means in quant.c, MSVC compiler will go through generic path when compiling. However, when I forcefully turn on this flag, I see an around 37% performance drop on CPU workloads. This is because MSVC already auto-vectorizes the generic C kernels when that header is not defined, defining the macros forces the compiler down the hand written intrinsics which is less performant.
### Future Works

While working on this, I found that `arm64-windows-llvm-release` is still just defaulting to cross compile for WoA. This actually automatically turn off `-DGGML_NATIVE` and does not actually enable some of the arm intrinsics that clang allows. 

I think we will need more profiling work into whether we should switch on `__NEON_ARM` for MSVC or we should just let MSVC to auto-vectorize the instructions. Especially when more missing NEON intrinsics are support in MSVC in the future.

title: CUDA: fuse dense Q4_K Gate/Up projections and SwiGLU for prefill
body:
## Overview

Quantize the shared input to Q8_1 once, compute Gate and Up in one CUDA kernel, and apply SwiGLU after the full K reduction. This removes duplicate activation quantization, FP32 projection-output round trips and the separate SwiGLU launch.
- Vectorized loads/stores: reduce memory-instruction overhead and use a bank-conflict-free shared-memory store mapping.
- Fusion-specific configuration: 64 rows and 128 threads per CTA, targeting two resident blocks per SM to balance resource usage and latency hiding. Actual residency depends on hardware and compiled resource usage.
- Existing code reused: Q8_1 quantization, scratch allocation, MMQ shared-memory layout, stock INT8 MMA with scale/min handling, async-copy helpers and existing graph-fusion safety checks.

Scope
Supports separate dense Q4_K Gate/Up weight tensors, F32 activations and split SwiGLU on supported NVIDIA Ampere-or-newer configurations. 
FP32 output and the subsequent quantization/Down projection are unchanged. HIP/MUSA retain their existing paths. GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1 disables the fusion

## Validation and performance
Result collected on the DGX Spark

title: Fix Unicode paths in Hugging Face cache
body:
## Overview

I fixed an issue on Windows that llama-server cannot recognize the Hugging Face Cache path which contains non-ASCII characters such as Japanese characters.

The file path 'std::filesystem::path' and the string 'std::string' were used interchangeably without the necessary UTF-8 conversion.

I followed the implementation policy in 'tool/server/server-tools.cpp':
"every crossing between a std::string (always UTF-8 here) and fs::path is converted explicitly".

I implemented the following behavior.

* Convert path names to UTF-8 when storing them as strings
* Use 'std::filesystem::u8path()' to convert from UTF-8 string to path names
* Use UTF-8 path name when checking whether cached files exist in the download process

I set the path containing the Japanese characters in the HF_HOME environment variable.
The llama-server found the correct path and successfully loaded the model from the cache.

## Additional information

### Reproduction

Place the folder in a path containing Japanese characters and then prepare the model data.
```
set HF_HOME=R:\お遊び新しいフォルダー\yc000g\hf
hf download unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-GGUF gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
```

The following command reproduces the error by loading the model in the Hugging Face cache:
```
llama-server.exe --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9931 -c 50000 -fa on --alias gemma-4-e4b --hf-repo unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-GGUF:Q4_K_XL --no-mmproj-auto
```

Before the fix, the error log:
```
0.00.760.267 E gguf_init_from_file: failed to open GGUF file 'R:\���V�ѐV�����t�H���_�[\yc000g\hf\hub\models--unsloth--gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-GGUF\snapshots\8c5a9e4fd5482e2be20fe0bf013b4c262a8f4265\gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf' (No such file or directory)
```

After the fix, the cache path works and the model loads correctly:
```
0.01.442.705 I srv    load_model: loading model 'unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-GGUF:Q4_K_XL'
0.04.729.649 I srv  llama_server: model loaded
0.04.729.656 I srv  llama_server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:9931
```
See 'log1.txt'.

For reference, this is a batch file that reproduces the problem before the fix: (Works on Japanese Windows)

test.bat
```
set HF_HOME=R:\お遊び新しいフォルダー\yc000g\hf
hf download unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-GGUF gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
llama-server.exe --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9931 -c 50000 -fa on --alias gemma-4-e4b --hf-repo unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-GGUF:Q4_K_XL --no-mmproj-auto
```

### Restrictions

Pathnames containing 4-byte UTF-8 characters such as emojis still do not work.
The cause has not been investigated.
See 'log2.txt'.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES

I use AI to investigate causes, isolate problems, consider corrective policies, and propose code.
After reviewing the proposed code myself and comparing it with existing similar parts (server-tools.cpp),
I update the source code, build it, check it works, and submit this pull request.

Thanks,

title: HIP : add shared-memory tiled transpose fast path for F32 concat on RDNA3.5
body:
## Overview

Add a narrowly gated shared-memory transpose path for F32 `CONCAT` on AMD
RDNA3.5. This targets a transposed input shape observed during Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
prefill input processing, for example:

```text
src0: [3,    8192]   contiguous
src1: [2048, 8192]   transposed F32 view
dst:  [2051, 8192]   concat(src0, src1), dim 0
```

The kernel uses 256 threads (`32 x 8`) and a padded shared-memory tile
`float tile[32][33]` to coalesce the transposed copy. The contiguous `src0`
portion is copied only by blocks with `blockIdx.y == 0`.

The fast path requires RDNA3.5, `dim == 0`, F32 inputs/output, input width
512/1024/2048, contiguous `src0` and `dst`, strict transpose strides for `src1`,
and a valid grid-z size. **It now also requires at least 64 output channels and
a channel count divisible by 32.** Small-channel and partial-channel-tile cases
use the existing implementation. This supersedes the small-channel regression
limitation described in the previous version of this PR.

Only `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/concat.cu` and `tests/test-backend-ops.cpp` change
(144 insertions, 1 deletion). Related to #21284.

## Additional information

### Revision and validation, 2026-09-23

- Tested base: `b1ff4ca23630ac7c5a275405353ddb5c486332c9`.
- Tested and submitted head: `e478c7ef9f81307f20d22a90256a802986f8bed6`.
- Windows 11, Radeon 8060S / gfx1151, ROCm 7.1; Release, HIP, MMQ MFMA,
  HIP Graphs, No VMM, UMA off, OpenMP off.
- Baseline and candidate `test-backend-ops` builds succeeded.
- Candidate CONCAT correctness: **272/272 twice**. The baseline with identical
  test registration also passed **272/272**. Transposed cases require
  bit-identical output via `std::memcmp`.

Coverage includes state widths 1/3/4; input widths 512/1024/2048; channel counts
31/32/33/64/65/96/97/128/129; `ne2 = 2`; the 8192-channel workload; and fallback
cases for non-whitelisted widths, contiguous F32 and transposed F16.

### Operator performance

A is the tested base plus the same test registration; B adds the production
kernel. After one warmup per version, the order was `A/B/B/A` repeated five
times: ten measured samples per version and shape. The shape is
`ne_a=[3,8192,1,1]`, `dim=0`, `v=16`.

| Input width | A median, microseconds | B median, microseconds | Latency reduction | B CV |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 185.985 | 59.095 | 68.23% | 0.43% |
| 1024 | 4237.470 | 498.305 | 88.24% | 1.43% |
| 2048 | 11100.610 | 1098.770 | 90.10% | 0.41% |

CV is the standard deviation divided by the mean. Baseline CV was 5.32% and
5.44% for widths 1024 and 2048 respectively; the table reports medians rather
than a best run. These are CONCAT operator measurements, **not end-to-end
model speedups**.

Commands after building each version, with ROCm DLLs on `PATH`:

```powershell
.\build-amd\bin\test-backend-ops.exe test -b ROCm0 -o CONCAT
.\build-amd\bin\test-backend-ops.exe perf -b ROCm0 -o CONCAT -p 'type=f32,ne_a=\[3,8192,1,1\].*v=16'
```

The baseline must include the same test-only changes so that both commands
exercise identical shapes.

### Scope and remaining validation

Earlier model-level measurements are historical evidence, not a rerun of this
exact head. Full-model reruns on September 14 were interrupted twice by
unexpected host reboots; the cause remains undetermined. No new end-to-end
performance claim is made for this revision. The current evidence is the
Windows build, CONCAT correctness and operator A/B above; other GPU
architectures have not been validated here.

The PR is already ready for review (`draft=false`), but the bot-added `draft`
label remains. The author account cannot remove it (GitHub returns HTTP 403).
Could a maintainer remove the stale label and check whether the relevant CI
needs approval? At the time of this update, only `labeler` had run successfully
for the new head.

title: cuda : accelerate conv2d with implicit GEMM
body:
## Overview

Accelerate the existing CUDA CONV_2D operator for F16 weights and F32 activations with a compact implicit-GEMM implementation. It uses a fixed 64x64x64 tile and the existing `mma.cuh` interface, with F32 accumulation, split-K for small spatial maps, and a cuBLAS path for eligible 1x1 convolutions.

The existing direct kernel remains the fallback, including F32 weights and small convolutions where conversion and launch overhead can outweigh the benefit. Three regression cases cover channel tails, multiple batches, stride/dilation, and the 1x1 path. The change is confined to `conv2d.cu` and the existing operator test file.

## Additional information

Existing work such as [#15805](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/15805) already explores implicit-GEMM convolution. This proposal focuses on keeping the implementation compact and straightforward to review: reuse the existing MMA primitives, use one tile configuration, keep the indexing and dispatch local, and retain the current fallback. The goal is to reduce review and maintenance overhead while providing useful acceleration.

Selected operator timings on an RTX 4090 with CUDA 12.4, Release, and CUDA graphs enabled, compared with `1af554f`. Input dimensions are [W,H,IC,N]; kernel dimensions are [KW,KH,IC,OC]. These are microbenchmarks, not end-to-end model results.

| F16 convolution | Before (us) | After (us) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| [58,58,32,1], [3,3,32,64] | 79.74 | 13.81 | 5.77x |
| [58,58,32,8], [3,3,32,64] | 500.27 | 41.84 | 11.96x |
| [16,16,128,8], [3,3,128,512] | 986.87 | 50.79 | 19.43x |
| [19,19,4,16], [2,2,4,4] | 4.38 | 4.42 | 0.99x |

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

title: ggml-metal: add Metal kernel for ggml_roll
body:
## Overview

Add a native Metal kernel for `GGML_OP_ROLL` (circular shift). This op currently has no Metal implementation, so it falls back to CPU on Apple Silicon, creating graph splits at every call site.

The Gemma 4 audio conformer uses two `ggml_roll` calls per layer across 12 layers, resulting in 73 graph splits on Metal. With this kernel, all conformer ops stay on the GPU.

The shader follows the same wrapping logic as the CPU implementation: for each element, compute the source index as `(dst_idx - shift) mod dim_size` per dimension.

**Files changed:**
- `ggml-metal-impl.h` - kargs struct
- `ggml-metal-device.m` - register `GGML_OP_ROLL` as supported
- `ggml-metal-device.cpp` - pipeline name mapping
- `ggml-metal-ops.h` - declare dispatch function
- `ggml-metal-ops.cpp` - dispatch function (sets args, binds buffers, dispatches threadgroups)
- `ggml-metal.metal` - `kernel_roll` shader

Ref: #21421 (Gemma 4 audio conformer PR where this was requested)

## Additional information

Tested locally on CPU (the logic matches). Needs validation on macOS Metal via CI or manual testing.

The dispatch uses the same pattern as `kernel_concat`: threadgroups over (ne01, ne02, ne03) with threads iterating over ne00.

# Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

title: server: Add support for binding to multiple addresses
body:
Binding `llama-server` to a VPN address currently makes it unavailable through localhost, breaking clients that default to localhost. Supporting multiple addresses lets one server remain accessible through both.

`--host` now accepts a comma-separated list of IP addresses and Unix socket paths. The server creates one listener per address, all serving the same API and model through a shared HTTP worker pool.

TCP listeners share the configured port. With `--port 0`, the first TCP listener selects an available port for the others. Every address must bind successfully; otherwise, startup fails and closes the listeners already bound. Each listening URL is logged separately.

title: cuda : improve top-k algorithm selection heuristic
body:
## Overview

This PR improves `ggml_top_k()` CUDA implementation algorithm selection heuristic based on tests results from https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/28547

## Additional information

Algorithm selection is performed in the following way:
```
NCOLS_THRESHOLD_BITONIC = 512
NCOLS_THRESHOLD_ARGSORT = 4096
NROWS_THRESHOLD_DEVICETOPK = 1

if ncols > NCOLS_THRESHOLD_BITONIC
    if nrows > NROWS_THRESHOLD_DEVICETOPK
        impl = radix
    else
        if DeviceTopK is available
            impl = DeviceTopK
        else
            if argsort is available
                if ncols > NCOLS_THRESHOLD_ARGSORT
                    impl = radix
                else
                    impl = argsort
            else
                impl = radix
else
    impl = bitonic
```

## Overview

Adds an optional Vulkan device-level keepalive for investigating #26196.

When enabled with `GGML_VK_KEEPALIVE_MS`, each Vulkan device periodically submits a minimal GPU operation to help prevent idle GPU memory eviction.

The feature is disabled by default and does not modify server sleep or `llama_synchronize()`.

## Additional information

This is a draft because I cannot reproduce the Intel B70/Windows issue locally. Testing on the affected hardware is needed to verify whether the keepalive prevents the reported VRAM drop and inference slowdown.

title: rfc: Memory eliding fusions
body:
## Overview

One of llama.cpp's strength is the availability of a variety of quantizations which reduce the memory usage and allow running quantized big models on modest hardware.

Running a qwen3.8-flash-next, I was surprised to see high memory usage of 2 GB of compute buffers on each card, which is a lot. This PR cuts compute buffer usage by more than a third in two steps, one of which is very invasive. Further reductions are possible, reducing compute buffer sizes to ~800MB per card on my setup, halving the current utilization.
The two steps are:
- Providing fusions to elide the memory requirements, fusing trivial operations with follow-up kernels
- (Invasive): Providing a callback to enable removal of "deleted" nodes.

| Device | Master | Allocator branch | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SYCL0 | 1893.85 MiB | 1173.85 MiB | 720.00 MiB (38.02%) |
| SYCL1 | 1901.10 MiB | 1181.10 MiB | 720.00 MiB (37.87%) |
| SYCL2 | 1901.10 MiB | 1181.10 MiB | 720.00 MiB (37.87%) |
| Total | 5696.05 MiB | 3536.05 MiB | 2160.00 MiB (37.92%) |
| SYCL host | 415.87 MiB | 415.87 MiB | 0 MiB |


<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
One of the key offenders of high memory usage are OP_CAST nodes, which currently expand the full ubatch into a buffer.

This branch extends the SYCL with support for eliding fused intermediate tensors:

- F16 cast plus F32 add fusion
- QSA score generation, ReLU, and head reduction fusion
- QSA gather fusion
- QSA gather, mask add, and radix top-k fusion

## Additional information


The removal of the buffer has only limited performance impact, because the sizes of the copied structures at 720MB are not prohibitive for GPUs which handle multiple hundred GB/s of throughput, and these operations are saturating this bandwidth.

| Metric | Master median | Allocator fusion median | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| pp16384 | 298.327 tok/s | 305.876 tok/s | +2.53% |
| tg16384 | 15.391 tok/s | 15.555 tok/s | +1.07% |
| pp65535 | 246.356 tok/s | 255.423 tok/s | +3.68% |
| tg65535| 8.830 tok/s | 8.885 tok/s | +0.62% |

However, it saves 720MB of buffers to create more headroom.

I'm not sure how to go about this; the change is very invasive because it needs to interact with the memory allocator to really reduce the number of compute buffers.  This is therefore more a basis for discussion / inspiration, as there are some fundamental dirty parts:
- The graph allocation / de-allocation is aimed to be as non-intrusive as possible, but still creates a bit of a mess
- The Fusions are HUGE, consuming multiple nodes, which may lead to increased maintenance efforts


Still, I believe being able to ditch compute buffers and reduce the insane dead copying from reshapes and casts by integrating them into fusions would help the project overall, and allow users to use the gained memory for MTP or more parallel processing. What are your feelings on this ( @arthw )?
Due to the massive change, I'm not sure this will ever be pulled, so I'm keeping it as a draft.

title: vulkan : reuse descriptor sets when bindings are constant
body:
## Overview

Descriptor sets come from a per-context ring whose cursor resets for every graph, so when the same graph is recorded again it already lands on the same set with the same buffers, offsets and ranges as last time. This keeps the last binding list written to each set and skips `vkUpdateDescriptorSets` when the new list is identical giving a 20-39% improved decode performance in translation layers and would be interesting to see how much it improves discrete GPU architectures broadly.

For the record, a skip keyed on `VkBuffer` handles alone is unsafe since a destroyed buffer's handle can be handed to a new buffer, and the set would still point at freed memory. As a result, the device counts buffer destroys and a context drops all of its cached bindings whenever that count has moved. This is coarse on purpose, since destroys are rare in steady-state decode. Without it, `test-backend-ops -b Vulkan0` fails 63 IM2COL_3D cases with ERR = inf and then crashes in TOP_K but with it, 18933 / 18933 pass.

To be clear, the gain depends on how expensive descriptor updates are for the driver. On MoltenVK on an Apple machine there was minimal to no benefit with 0 regression.

Perplexity on wikitext-2 is identical to master, all 569 chunks.

`GGML_VK_DISABLE_DESCRIPTOR_REUSE=1` is a flag that can disable this patch and is read once on device creation.

## Requirements

## Overview

An opt-in `--no-fallback` flag for llama-quantize that will exit with an error when tensor shapes would otherwise force a
fallback quant - before any tensor data is read. More information can be found in the issue #26616 with related
discussion.

- Opt-in flag on `llama-quantize`. When any tensor shape would force a type substitution, it errors out before any
  tensor data is read, through the same error path the `imatrix` check uses, so the tool exits non-zero
- Why a flag: dry run reports the substitutions but cannot gate on them. `--dry-run --no-fallback` is a preflight check
  that finishes in seconds

      lines are unchanged

  members after it shift so any code built with the old struct layout must rebuild; identical trade to

title: sycl: accelerate GLM MLA prefill with MKL flash attention
body:
## Overview

- route GLM-4.7 Flash's `DKQ=576`, `DV=512`, GQA-20 F16 MLA prompt shape through the existing SYCL MKL flash-attention pipeline
- correctly handle V as a narrower, strided view of the K cache
- keep the exception narrowly restricted to the validated GLM shape
- add an exact backend test for the newly supported layout

## Additional information

### Problem

The normal SYCL MKL flash-attention gate requires matching K and V head dimensions and limits the head dimension to 512.

GLM-4.7 Flash uses:

- Q head width: 576
- K head width: 576
- V head width: 512
- Q heads: 20
- KV heads: 1
- K/V type: F16

Because `DKQ != DV` and `DKQ > 512`, GLM prefill falls back to the generic TILE kernel. That fallback scales poorly with context length and causes severe long-context prefill degradation.

The existing MKL pipeline already parameterizes the KQ and VKQ operations with separate dimensions, so it can support this shape once dispatch and V-cache layout handling are corrected.

### Implementation

The new dispatch exception is deliberately narrow. It admits only:

- `Q = 576`
- `K = 576`
- `V = 512`
- GQA = 20
- F16 K and V

All existing prompt, mask, bias, softcap, batch, graph, and cache restrictions remain in force. Other unequal K/V shapes continue to use their existing fallback paths.

GLM stores V as a 512-element sub-view of a 576-element K-cache row. Its logical row is 1,024 bytes, while its physical row stride remains 1,152 bytes.

The implementation therefore:

- selects the strided F16 descriptor when a KV row has padding
- accepts the unusual V stride only when V is a real view sharing K's row stride
- aliases K and V dequantization buffers only when their logical dimensions match
- keeps unrelated attention shapes on their existing paths

An exact backend test covers the 576/512, GQA-20, strided-V configuration.

### Performance

Intel Arc Pro B70, IntelLLVM 2026.1, oneDNN enabled, F16 KV, `-ngl 999 -b 4096 -ub 1024 -fa on`, three repetitions.

This table compares clean master with this standalone patch only.

#### Prompt processing

| Prompt | Master | Patched | Improvement |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 1,283.35 tok/s | 1,284.97 tok/s | +0.13% |
| 8,192 | 429.28 tok/s | 1,293.63 tok/s | 3.01x, +201.35% |
| 64,000 | 67.071 tok/s | 378.145 tok/s | 5.64x, +463.80% |

The improvement grows with context length because the patch removes GLM's quadratic TILE fallback and routes the supported MLA shape through MKL flash attention.

#### Context-loaded generation

Generation of 256 tokens after preloading the stated KV-cache depth:

| Depth | Master | Patched | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 45.029 tok/s | 45.089 tok/s | +0.13% |
| 8,192 | 32.596 tok/s | 32.636 tok/s | +0.12% |
| 64,000 | 11.766 tok/s | 11.778 tok/s | +0.10% |

Generation remains effectively unchanged, as expected for a prompt-processing dispatch change.

### Validation

- applies cleanly to current upstream master `b23efaa2`
- Release IntelLLVM 2026.1 SYCL build succeeds with oneDNN, F16, graphs, and Level Zero support
- exact GLM MLA backend case passes: 1/1
- debug output confirms MKL dispatch with `D=576`, `DV=512`, 20 Q heads, and one KV head
- complete SYCL0 `FLASH_ATTN_EXT` suite: 4,044/4,045 passed
- the sole failure is the existing Q8_0 permuted-layout case, reproduced on the unmodified baseline
- `git diff --check` passes

### Scope

This is a standalone three-file change:

- `ggml/src/ggml-sycl/fattn.cpp`
- `ggml/src/ggml-sycl/fattn-mkl.cpp`
- `tests/test-backend-ops.cpp`

It does not depend on the IQ3 optimization, the MMVQ decode fusions, PR #28918, PR #28931, or any other B70 campaign patch.

title: vulkan: hide internal symbols to prevent duplicate-dlopen state destr…
body:
## Overview
               
 Build the ggml-vulkan target with hidden symbol visibility so that only the public API (explicitly marked `GGML_BACKEND_API`) is exported.             
                                                                               
 Fixes #29138                                                               
                
## Additional information
    
Since #28732 the backend's internal cross-TU symbols (`vk_instance`,  `ggml_vk_init`, ...) are exported with default visibility. If a duplicate copy of the library is dlopened and dlclosed in the same process — which  `ggml_backend_load_all()` does when `libggml-vulkan.so` in the executable directory is a regular-file copy instead of a symlink (`cp`/`scp` dereference symlinks) — ELF symbol interposition makes the duplicate's static destructors  destroy the live library's `vk_instance`. rpc-server/llama-server then crash  at startup on `GGML_ASSERT(... < vk_instance.device_indices.size())`.        
                                                                                 
Hiding the internal symbols restores the pre-#28732 behavior where a   duplicate dlopen/dlclose is harmless.

title: server : do not expose the media marker in /props, escape stray markers in chat text
body:
## Overview

`GET /props` currently returns the live `media_marker` value. The marker is a random per-process string that the server uses to splice image/audio/video parts into rendered prompts, and the tokenizer requires the marker count to match the bitmap count exactly.
If the marker string ends up in the conversation text - e.g. an agent stores the /props response as tool output and replays it on every turn - every subsequent request fails with 400 "Failed to tokenize prompt", and the session is stuck forever because the poisoned message stays in the history.

Fixes #29118, #25285.

Changes:
- remove `media_marker` from the /props output (and from the README example). 
Native clients that place markers in `prompt_string` can pin the marker with the `LLAMA_MEDIA_MARKER` env var (noted in the README);
- escape stray marker occurrences in user-provided chat text (raw-string content and `text` content parts) to an inert `<__media_literal__>` placeholder, so only the markers the server itself injected for real media parts reach the tokenizer;
- add server tests: /props no longer exposes the field, a stray marker in the text does not fail tokenization (with or without an image), and the native "marker count must match bitmap count" contract is still enforced for user-placed markers.

Compared to #27375 (closed): the tokenizer still errors when bitmaps outnumber markers (a real image would be dropped), and stray markers in chat text are replaced by a readable placeholder before tokenization instead of being fed to the model as literal marker text.

## Additional information

Repro (before the fix), from #29118:

```bash
MARKER=$(curl -s http://localhost:8080/props | jq -r .media_marker)
curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"x\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"$MARKER\"}],\"max_tokens\":8}"
# 400 Failed to tokenize prompt
```

The tests pin the marker with `LLAMA_MEDIA_MARKER` (already used in `test_vision_api.py`) so they are deterministic.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

title: sycl: FWHT kernels for block widths above 512
body:
The SYCL FWHT covers 64 to 512 via the standard butterfly network, plus 384/640/768/1280 via the Kronecker/Paley construction added separately in #28016. Neither path covers the pure power-of-2 widths above 512 that the Hadamard hint can produce (1024, 2048, 4096, 8192); those still fall through to the default case and run as a dense GEMM against the materialized rotation tensor, correct but O(n^2) instead of O(n log n).

fwht_kernel_wide runs one row per work-group instead of per sub-group, so each work-item keeps N/NT values rather than N/WARP_SIZE. Butterflies below the sub-group width still shuffle; those up to the work-group width go through work-group local memory; the rest stay in registers. Same butterfly and sign convention as the existing narrow kernel.

Verification note: I don't have access to an Intel GPU, and ggml's SYCL backend registration (dpct::dev_mgr) requires a GPU-labeled platform to exist before any op can run, so test-backend-ops couldn't be exercised end to end even via the CPU device. I verified the kernel algorithm itself with a standalone harness on a real SYCL CPU device (Intel oneAPI DPC++ 2026.1), checked against an independent Hadamard reference, and cross-validated the harness by first confirming it correctly passes the existing unmodified narrow kernel. All four widths pass, single- and multi-row. Full numbers in the commit message. The build itself is verified (fwht.cpp compiles clean as part of ggml-sycl), but the ggml dispatch/supports_op integration has not been exercised on real hardware. Happy to have someone with an Arc GPU (or other SYCL-capable GPU) confirm before merge.

## Overview

<!-- TODO(author): describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
- `ggml_cuda_fattn_kv_type_supported` now accepts `GGML_TYPE_IQ4_NL` as a KV cache type, together with the dequantization counterpart the flash attention kernels use to read that cache: `dequantize_iq4_nl_pair` and the `to_fp16_nc_cuda` / `to_bf16_nc_cuda` / `to_fp32_nc_cuda` dispatch entries for `IQ4_NL`. This makes `-ctk iq4_nl -ctv iq4_nl -fa on` work instead of falling back.
- On MUSA, `FLASH_ATTN_AVAILABLE` is a property of the compilation pass rather than of the device: `__MUSA_ARCH__` is only defined in the device pass, so in every host pass the old condition removed the FA device code from the translation unit, and availability was decided at runtime today. The MUSA part of the guard is now additionally conditioned on `defined(__MUSA_ARCH__)`, and [the runtime check in the host code] rejects devices whose MUSA architecture has no FA device code (only `QY2` / `mp_22` and later have it).

The first change affects CUDA as well; the second is MUSA specific and does not change behaviour on devices that have FA code, such as the MTT S5000 (`mp_31`) used below.

title: musa: fix PH1 (MTT S5000) operator failures and build issues
body:
## Overview
PH1 (MTT S5000, MUSA architecture `31`) is the current MUSA target, but parts of the CUDA backend still assumed the first generation (MTT S80, `21`) or carried compile-time workarounds for older MUSA toolkits. This series lets those paths use the upstream code and fixes the operator failures that `test-backend-ops` reports on an MTT S5000 with MUSA SDK 5.2.0:
- **build and enablement** — 16-byte copies like `sm_70` and up, the CUB based paths, the cooperative launch query and the device warp size, `CUDA_SET_SHARED_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `cudaFuncSetAttribute`, and MUSA-only guards that a runtime architecture check already covers
- **operator fixes** — the `q8_0` dequantization kernel was compiled out on MUSA (moved to #29292), the fused `TOPK_MOE` kernel could hang in `__syncthreads()`, `MMQ` computes wrong values on PH1, `GATED_DELTA_NET` is enabled
- **flash attention** — availability is decided from the runtime compute capability, and `IQ4_NL` is supported as a KV cache type (moved to #29293)
- **graphs** — the stream capture query API is aliased for MUSA, so a `-DGGML_MUSA_GRAPHS=ON` build compiles

title: vulkan: GEMM/Group GEMM optimizations on Intel Xe (3/3, Xe-LPG Plus/Xe2/Xe3)
body:
## Overview

**Co-authors:** @jxia4intel, @sliu39

**PR 3/3** of the Intel Xe optimization series — see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24408 (mega PR, draft) for the full feature set.

**Target platforms:** Xe-LPG Plus, Xe2, Xe3

This PR adds GEMM/Group GEMM kernel optimizations and load-time weight compression for the Intel quick MoE path. Dependency: builds on top of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24404 (Xe-LPG Plus coopmat1 enable). Independent of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24406 (FA).

### GEMM kernel optimizations (Intel Xe)

- `LOAD_A_OPT` path: SLM-based A-matrix layout optimization for coopmat1
- MXFP4, Q4_K, Q5_K dequant via `bitfieldExtract` optimization
- Alt pipeline (`l_alt`/`a_l_alt`, BM=128 warptile) for runtime selection when problem dimensions are small
- f32→f16 activation conversion for Intel coopmat GEMM, scoped to Intel devices only
- `vulkan-shaders-gen.cpp`: registers all new pipeline variants

### MoE optimizations (Intel Xe)

- `mul_mm.comp` shader optimization for `MUL_MAT_ID`: reduces unnecessary memory loads and matrix core operations for MoE models
- Separate warptile tuning for MoE expert GEMM
- Gemma4 MoE router: fuse `rms_norm + mul` into a single `RMS_NORM_MUL` kernel dispatch for the expert gate input calculation

title: model : re-enable -sm tensor for qwen4exp
body:
## Overview

Re-enables `-sm tensor` for qwen4exp. #27941 disabled it because `test-llama-archs -a qwen4exp` asserted on the Meta device once the fixture carried a PLE layer, and removed the test's earlier Meta skip for the arch.

The abort is a scheduler placement, not QSA. `test-llama-archs` builds the model with the embeddings host-resident, so the PLE embedding gather (`ggml_get_rows` on `per_layer_token_embd`) is a CPU node. In the qwen4exp graph `hc_init` (the `ggml_repeat_4d` that fans the embedding out to the hc streams) is first materialised inside layer 0's PLE path, after that gather. `ggml_backend_sched_split_graph` pass 2 expands a device assignment upwards only until it meets a CPU-assigned node, so the REPEAT is never reached from the first Meta node and "expand rest" leaves it on the CPU. The later `ggml_reshape_3d(hc_init)` inside the PLE query norm is then a view of a host-resident node inside the meta split, which `ggml_backend_meta_graph_compute` only tolerates for `view_src->op == GGML_OP_NONE`: `GGML_ASSERT(ggml_backend_buffer_is_meta(tensor->buffer))` at ggml-backend-meta.cpp:476. deepseek4 builds the same hc init but its REPEAT is followed directly by a weight matmul, so the expansion reaches it.

Fix: `ggml_build_forward_expand(gf, res_hc)` right after `hc_init` is built. The REPEAT then directly precedes the first device node and pass 2 assigns it there; the embedding reshape stays in the CPU split and is copied in as a split input, the same shape deepseek4's graph has.

`test-llama-archs` on this branch (master e6ab7c1a4 + the change; seed 4097205655; RelWithDebInfo, RADV gfx1151, Mesa 25.2.8):

| arch | Vulkan | Meta (-sm tensor) |
|---|---|---|
| qwen4exp | OK (1.17e-07) | OK (1.17e-07), was GGML_ASSERT |
| deepseek4 | OK (8.44e-07) | OK (8.44e-07) |
| qwen35 | OK (8.33e-08) | OK (8.33e-08) |

Real model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, `-sm tensor` over two RPC devices (#26610 tree with this change, one Vulkan `ggml-rpc-server` per Strix Halo box, ctx 65536) vs a single device, greedy: byte-identical on a short prompt and on a 1.8k-token prompt (1752 generated tokens), and identical to master's single-device output.

title: sycl: add grouped MoE XMX GEMM
body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
The current approach to handling experts in MoE models use one GEMM per expert. These activations are relatively narrow, and cannot use the compute hardware effectively (neither ALU0/1 nor the XMX tiles). Additionally, the small inputs result in particularly inefficient dequantization. 
This can be fixed by grouping many small experts into one kernel, and handling them in one operation.

This patch proposes grouped and optionally fused GEMM kernels tuned on XMX (`joint_matrix`).
Approach:
- Build a host-side schedule of active expert tiles and launch as one grouped kernel instead of one GEMM per expert
- Dequantizes IQ4_NL or IQ3_S weights into f16 tiles in local memory
- Packs routed f32 activations into the VNNI f16 layout consumed by XMX.

## Additional information
Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF:UD-IQ4_XS`.
The boost happens during pp.

body:
Overview
This PR addresses cold-start race conditions and queueing behavior under concurrency limits:
Slot Reservation & Queuing: Ensures concurrent requests reserve model slots while holding the scheduler lock, enforcing queuing as soon as the model limit is reached.
Eviction Protection: Shares load across requests targeting the same model, keeping newly loaded models protected from eviction until the waiting request explicitly claims ownership.
Timeout Fix: Replaced an overly short 30-second test timeout with the standard suite budget to fix test stalls caused by Metal shader compilation.

title: Add SYCL graph record and replay
body: ## Overview This is a port of the existing CUDA graph code to SYCL. The code is mostly a straight port with two SYCL-specific exceptions: 1. The data must be reordered before recording because while SYCL async memory allocation extensions are available, using them leads to a hang during graph recording. 2. The library GEMM functions don't work with graph recording because it throws an exception: "Graph nodes cannot depend on events from outside the graph." This effectively limits the feature to decode for the time being. On A770 the performance improvement during decode is significant; on B70 it is negligible. Thus the feature remains off by default. ## Additional information While investigating performance differences on A770 between the Vulkan and SYCL backends, I found that kernel dispatch time consumed a large percentage of the SYCL time. The large difference was primarily due to the usage of the i915 driver. However there is still a modest gain with the xe driver. ### A770 performance comparison **xe driver** **i915 driver** ## Requirements - I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) - AI usage disclosure: YES. title: llama: GPU-resident LRU cache for host-offloaded MoE expert weights
body:
## Summary

GPU-resident LRU cache for MoE expert weights that live in host memory (via `-ot ...exps=CPU`, `-ncmoe`, etc.). Decode on a host-offloaded MoE layer is bound by host RAM bandwidth: every token streams the routed experts' weights from system RAM. This PR serves the *recently used* experts from VRAM instead.

Opt-in via `--moe-expert-cache N` (slots per host-resident expert layer; `--moe-expert-cache-inserts` caps uploads per layer per decode step). Fully inert when disabled.

## Motivation / measurements

Measured on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL (512 experts, 10 routed/token, 28 expert layers pinned to host by `-ot`), 2x RTX 3090 + dual-Xeon host (single populated RAM channel per socket):

- Routing was instrumented over a 54k-record mixed workload (code / math / prose / multilingual):
  - **No exploitable static skew**: a top-32 "hot expert" list learned on half the workload covers only ~10% of the other half (uniform = 6.2%). Static pinning of experts is a dead end.
  - **Strong temporal locality**: a per-layer LRU-64 would hit ~67%, LRU-128 ~81%. This is what the cache exploits.
- End-to-end decode: **18.4 -> 24.2 tok/s** (+31%) with 48 slots/layer (~4.1 GiB VRAM) at 2 uploads/layer/step.
- Overhead when enabled but cold is ~zero (measured with uploads disabled).

## Mechanism (no new CUDA kernels)

- Per cached layer: companion tensors `[ne0, ne1, K+1]` for up/gate/down in the device buffer of that layer's router. Slot `K` is permanently zero (the "dummy" slot).
- An I32 `expert id -> slot` table per layer, two copies:
  - device copy: `ggml_get_rows` remaps `selected_experts` into slot ids for a **second `mul_mat_id` chain** over the cache tensors. Uncached ids map to the zero slot and contribute exactly 0.
  - host copy: passed as `src[3]` to the **CPU** `mul_mat_id`, which skips cached ids and zeroes their dst rows.
- The two down-projection outputs are summed - the split is exact by construction (each expert is computed on exactly one side).
- Decode-only (`n_tokens == 1`); batches/prefill build the stock graph, so batch offload is untouched.
- Updates are throttled and **asynchronous**: evictions are published at a decode-boundary sync point, slices are copied by a worker thread via `ggml_backend_tensor_set`, and the new mapping is only published at a later sync point after the copy completed - a running graph can never read a torn slot. (Synchronous uploads were measured to eat the entire win.)

## Known discussion points (why this is a draft)

- The cache is a per-process singleton keyed by the `up_exps` tensor pointer, because `build_moe_ffn` has no model access. Happy to rework the ownership (e.g. hang it off `llama_model`) per your preference.
- The CPU `mul_mat_id` observation callback (`ggml_set_moe_obs_callback`) is a ggml -> llama upcall; suggestions for a cleaner layering welcome.
- Only the separate gate/up + `LLM_FFN_SILU` path is wired; other MoE variants fall back to the stock graph.
- Multi-token decode (speculative/MTP) currently bypasses the cache (`n_tokens == 1` guard); extending the remap to small batches is straightforward if the approach is acceptable.
- The routing-locality result should transfer to other MoE models (uniform aggregate usage but high temporal locality is what load-balancing losses + real text produce), but only Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has been measured.

## Testing

- A/B benchmarks above; outputs coherent over thousands of tokens at 48-81% measured hit rates.
- `test-arg-parser` argument section passes (the URL/404 section fails in my sandbox for network reasons, unrelated).
- Will add a runtime smoke of the final CLI plumbing before marking ready for review.

title: qwen35 : support d2t draft-vocab trim for MTP draft models
body:
## Summary

FastMTP-style MTP draft models (e.g. a 32K-draft-vocab variant of Qwen3.8-27B) store
the draft MTP output projection over a **reduced draft vocabulary**, together with a
`d2t` (draft-to-target) index tensor mapping draft-vocab rows to full-vocab rows.

Before this change, a qwen35 MTP-only model containing a `d2t` tensor could not be
loaded: the MTP `output.weight` is sized `{n_embd, n_draft_vocab}` while the loader
expected `{n_embd, n_vocab}`.

The change mirrors the existing `d2t` handling in `eagle3.cpp` / `dflash.cpp`:

- `load_arch_tensors`: when loading the MTP part and a `d2t` tensor is present, load
  the output projection at the draft-vocab size (`d2t->ne[0]`).
- `graph_mtp`: scatter the draft logits into the full vocabulary with `ggml_set_rows`
  (uncovered full-vocab rows stay `-inf`), emitting the result as `result_output_d2t`
  in addition to `result_output`. `res->t_logits` ends up pointing at the full-vocab
  logits, which the speculative-decoding acceptance path needs.

## Testing

Verified with `--spec-type draft-mtp` + a 32K-draft-vocab qwen35 GGUF
(Qwen3.8-27B, dual RTX 5070 Ti): the draft model loads, MTP acceptance works, and
generation quality is unaffected.

title: Possible fix: use ne0..ne3 (dst dims) instead of ne00..ne03 in ggml_compute_forward_dup_f16
body:
I might have found a small mistake in ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp, in the non-contiguous path of ggml_compute_forward_dup_f16 when dst->type == GGML_TYPE_F16.

The carry after each element uses ne00/ne01/ne02/ne03 (source dims). Since the indices i10..i13 point to dst, I think it should compare against ne0/ne1/ne2/ne3 (destination dims). The adjacent F32 branch seems to use ne0..ne3.

Apologies if I’m missing context. If this intentional, feel free to close.

title: feat(qwen35): support d2t draft-vocabulary trim for MTP speculative decoding
body:
## Overview

This PR adds support for trimmed/compact draft vocabularies via the `d2t` (draft-to-target) mapping tensor in both `qwen35` and `qwen35moe` model architectures during MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) speculative decoding.

When loading an MTP draft model or sidecar trained with a reduced draft vocabulary (such as FastMTP / compact speculative heads), the LM head (`output.weight` or `layer.nextn.shared_head_head`) has dimensions `[n_embd, n_draft_vocab]` where `n_draft_vocab < n_vocab`. Previously, `llama_model_qwen35` and `llama_model_qwen35moe` unconditionally initialized output projections with `n_vocab`, causing loader dimension mismatches or runtime assertion failures.

With this PR:
1. When `d2t` is present, `output` and `layer.nextn.shared_head_head` are initialized with the draft vocabulary dimension `n_vocab_out = d2t->ne[0]`.
2. Fallback to `output = create_tensor(tn(LLM_TENSOR_TOKEN_EMBD), ...)` is prevented when `d2t` is present and an explicit draft head is provided.
3. In `graph_mtp`, draft candidate logits of shape `[n_draft_vocab, n_outputs]` are scattered onto a full-vocabulary `-inf` tensor of shape `[n_vocab_full, n_outputs]` using `ggml_set_rows`, consistent with existing `dflash.cpp` and `eagle3.cpp` implementations.
4. Validation assertions confirm that draft vocabulary dimensions match the active LM head.

---

## Technical Details

### 1. Root Cause
In standard MTP, the next-n prediction head shares the full vocabulary (`n_vocab = 152064` for Qwen 3.5). However, high-throughput speculative decoding optimizations often prune the draft vocabulary to the most frequent tokens (e.g. 32,768 tokens) mapped by a `d2t` tensor.
- Without `d2t` handling, `load_arch_tensors` expected `[n_embd, 152064]`, causing GGUF tensor loading failure (`tensor 'blk.0.nextn.shared_head_head.weight' size mismatch`).
- If fallback occurred, `tok_embd` was assigned to `output`, clobbering the compact draft head with target embedding weights.

### 2. Implementation
- **Detection:** `load_arch_tensors` inspects `ml.get_tensor_meta("d2t")` when `mtp_only` is true.
- **Tensors:** `output` and `layer.nextn.shared_head_head` allocate `n_vocab_out` rows.
- **Logits Projection:** In `graph_mtp`, after `cur = build_lora_mm(head_w, cur, head_s)`:
  ```cpp
  if (model.d2t) {
      const int64_t n_draft_vocab = cur->ne[0];
      const int64_t n_outputs     = cur->ne[1];
      const int64_t n_vocab_full  = (int64_t) model.vocab.n_tokens();

      GGML_ASSERT(model.d2t->ne[0] == n_draft_vocab);

      ggml_tensor * logits = ggml_fill(ctx0,
              ggml_new_tensor_3d(ctx0, GGML_TYPE_F32, 1, n_vocab_full, n_outputs), -INFINITY);
      cur = ggml_set_rows(ctx0, logits,
              ggml_reshape_3d(ctx0, cur,       1,             n_draft_vocab, n_outputs),
              ggml_reshape_3d(ctx0, model.d2t, n_draft_vocab, 1,             1));
      cur = ggml_reshape_2d(ctx0, cur, n_vocab_full, n_outputs);
      cb(cur, "result_output_d2t", -1);
  }
  ```

---

## Benchmarks & Verification

Tested on dual NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Ada / Blackwell GPUs running live inference:
- **Baseline (Autoregressive dense decoding):** ~44.5 tokens/sec (22.47 ms/token).
- **With FastMTP Draft-Vocab Trim:** **102.2 – 113.9 tokens/sec** (**8.78 – 9.84 ms/token**).
- **Speedup:** **~2.3x – 2.5x throughput improvement** with up to **82.89%** draft acceptance rate.
- **Compilation:** Clean build verified on GCC 13.3, Clang 18, and NVCC CUDA 12.0/13.3.

---

## Authors & Attribution
- **Sreesanth R** ([@Shreesh-Sree](https://github.com/Shreesh-Sree))
- **Allen Joseph** ([@unknownhackerworld](https://github.com/unknownhackerworld))

---

title: cuda : add conv3d with implicit GEMM
body:
## Overview

Add CUDA support for `GGML_OP_CONV_3D`, used by `ggml_conv_3d_direct`, with an F16 implicit-GEMM kernel and a direct fallback for F32 weights and shapes outside the fast path. Inputs and outputs are contiguous F32 tensors; weights can be F16 or F32.

There are already CUDA conv3d proposals, including [#16948](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/16948), [#17255](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/17255), and [#24569](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24569). This PR offers a compact implementation intended to make the indexing, bounds checks, and performance tradeoffs easier to review and maintain. It reuses `mma.cuh`, uses one fixed 64x64x64 tile shape, and keeps the convolution indexing and dispatch in one source file. The goal is to lower the review burden around this operation.
